project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
A European community of practice that develops and maintains shared data, analytics and open-source tools for running grids with high shares of renewables.
A community of practice is a lasting network in which grid operators, researchers, technology providers and other energy actors work together on common tools. This is a coordination and support action: the project organises cooperation, innovation hubs, blueprints and repositories, rather than doing research itself.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
Projects are expected to cover all six activities the call lists; the call marks none as optional or excluded.
- Coordinate key actors in the energy value chain (grid operators, research and academia, technology and solution providers, energy suppliers, providers of energy services on markets, consumer representatives) into a community of practice on data and analytics for planning, operating and maintaining European grids with high shares of renewables
- Involve, cooperate or build synergies with major European and international initiatives active in this field
- Create a European ecosystem of innovation hubs where energy stakeholders collaborate on digitalisation projects, with space for experimentation and agile innovation
- Showcase targeted cooperation between grid operators and research and academia on specific projects or programmes
- Build blueprints, methodologies and repositories of open-source solutions for simulation, observation, forecasting, asset management and decision-making, to reduce the overall cost of system operation
- Promote modern solutions such as digital twins (live virtual models of the grid) and AI-enabled systems
Because it is a coordination and support action, research and innovation activities themselves are not eligible.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 14 · B — Eligible activities, Coordination and support actions

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
European grid operators and researchers lack coordinated, shared and maintained data-driven tools for grids with high shares of renewables.
The need originates with grid operators and the research community: planning and simulation tools, data and open-source software are fragmented, and research results are often not kept findable and reusable after projects end. The call wants this solved through EU-wide cooperation, so that tools are available to research, academia, grid operators and other actors in the energy value chain.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Expected Outcome

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
A working community of practice, a network of innovation hubs, and blueprints, methodologies and open-source repositories for data-driven grid tools.
- A community of practice of energy value-chain actors
- A European ecosystem of innovation hubs for digitalisation projects
- Blueprints, methodologies and repositories of open-source solutions for simulation, observation, forecasting, asset management and decision-making
- New open-source solutions and software modules added to existing or new repositories
- Showcases of cooperation between grid operators and research
- Support to keep research results FAIR (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable) after projects end
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
Projects must contribute to all six expected outcomes, centred on EU-wide cooperation and open-source tools for grid planning and operation.
- Enhanced EU cooperation and knowledge sharing on data and analytics for grid planning, operation and market integration
- Better EU coordination of planning and simulation tools for grid development and renewable integration, made available to research, grid operators and the energy value chain
- Coordinated processes that generate new open-source solutions and software modules for repositories supporting grids with high shares of renewables
- Improved EU-wide cooperation on data-driven solutions for energy, including AI-powered tools
- Support for researchers to keep results FAIR beyond the end of their projects
- Promotion of open-source practice across the energy sector to industrialise shared methods and standards
A further aim named in the scope is to reduce the overall cost of system operation. The call sets no quantified targets.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
The whole point is lasting use: the community, repositories and FAIR results must outlive individual projects.
- The call asks for a community of practice focused on developing and maintaining key tools, which implies continuity beyond the grant
- Results must stay FAIR beyond the end of research projects, accommodating technology evolution
- Open-source practice should foster industrialisation of shared methods and standards in the energy industry
- Selected projects are expected to contribute to BRIDGE (the European Commission's cooperation network of smart-grid, storage and digital energy projects)
The call does not say who must finance or run the community after the project.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
A single organisation may apply; there is no minimum or maximum consortium size.
For a coordination and support action, a proposal may be submitted by one or more legal entities established in an EU Member State or a country associated with Horizon Europe (non-EU countries taking part in the programme). The topic expects about one project.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · B — Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 12 · B — Coordination and Support Actions

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
The call names no mandatory partner types, but the community must bring together the whole energy value chain.
The actors to involve are grid operators, research and academia, technology and solution providers, energy suppliers, energy service providers and consumer representatives. Beneficiaries must be established in an EU Member State or Associated Country; organisations from other countries can only be associated partners. Entities assessed as high-risk suppliers of mobile network communication equipment, and entities they own or control, are excluded under the restriction for the protection of European communication networks.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Specific conditions and Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 7–9 · B — Restrictions for the protection of European communication networks
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 12 · B — Coordination and Support Actions

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
The call prescribes no division of work or budget among partners.
Since this is a lump sum grant (a fixed amount paid against completed work packages), the consortium must allocate the lump sum to work packages and partners in a detailed budget table. The call does ask for targeted cooperation between grid operators and research and academia to be showcased.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Specific conditions and Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, lump sum grant proposals

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
No type of organisation is prescribed: the beneficiaries choose one of themselves as coordinator.
The coordinator manages and coordinates the project and represents the consortium towards the granting authority (the European Commission or its agency). At submission it must confirm that it has the mandate to act for all applicants.
For a single-applicant proposal, that applicant is automatically the coordinator.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, Submission
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · B — Consortium composition

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Yes: TenneT TSO B.V. may coordinate or even apply alone, since any eligible entity in a Member State may lead a coordination and support action.
The scope puts grid operators first among the actors to bring together, so a TSO-led community is consistent with the call. Coordinating would mean managing the network and representing the consortium towards the European Commission.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 12–13 · B — Coordination and Support Actions, Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Scope

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes, as an associated partner, which takes part without funding and bears its own costs.
An associated partner does not sign the grant agreement, cannot charge costs, does not need legal validation and does not count towards the minimum of three beneficiaries from three countries. It must still register in the Participant Register before the application is submitted.
Grid operators are named as key actors in the community, so TenneT could also join the community's activities without being in the consortium at all.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Eligibility, Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration, Consortium roles and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes: as a beneficiary TenneT can receive funding covering up to 100% of its eligible costs, paid as part of a lump sum.
This topic is a coordination and support action (a project that networks, coordinates or supports others, without research work of its own), for which the maximum rate is 100% for all participants, including companies. The grant is a lump sum: the funding rate is already built into the amount, which is paid against completed work packages rather than reported costs. The expected EU contribution is around EUR 6 million for the whole project. The call sets no Dutch national rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Specific conditions

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer:
TenneT could bring the TSO perspective and its digital twin collaborations into the community, and host or co-lead a Dutch innovation hub.
This is our interpretation. TenneT already works on shared digital tools with Delft University of Technology in the National Facility Digital Twin of the Electricity System, supports the NWO programme Unlocking Digital Twin Capabilities for Electricity Utilities, and takes part in TwinEU and the TSO Innovation Alliance. These are exactly the kind of grid-operator and research cooperation the call wants showcased, and could feed blueprints and open-source repositories for planning, forecasting and asset management.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer:
No new research is required: the project coordinates, shares and maintains tools, and research activities are outside a coordination and support action.
The call does expect coordinated processes that generate new open-source solutions and software modules, but as outputs of the community rather than as research work of the project.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Expected Outcome
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 14 · B — Eligible activities, Coordination and support actions

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer:
The innovation is mainly in governance and cooperation models: a community of practice, innovation hubs, blueprints and open-source practice.
The technical content concerns data, analytics, simulation, forecasting, asset management and decision-making tools, including digital twins and AI.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Coordination, networking and dissemination; the call does not ask for research, prototyping or demonstration.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: No demonstration is required; the call asks for innovation hubs as spaces for experimentation and for showcases of cooperation.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Scope

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer:
The project must connect with existing initiatives and repositories rather than build in isolation.
It must involve or build synergies with major European and international initiatives in the field, add solutions to existing or new repositories, and contribute to BRIDGE.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer:
Users are the community itself: grid operators, consumers' representatives and other energy actors must be brought together.
The call names grid operators, research and academia, technology and solution providers, energy suppliers, providers of energy services and representatives of consumers.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Scope

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer:
The call sets no cybersecurity requirement for the tools, but excludes high-risk communication-equipment suppliers.
- Communication networks: entities assessed as high-risk suppliers of mobile network communication equipment, and entities they own or control, may not be beneficiaries, affiliated entities or associated partners
- Satellite data: if the project uses satellite-based earth observation, positioning, navigation or timing data, it must use Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS (the EU satellite systems)
cards.sources:

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
One project of around EUR 6 million is expected, which is the whole topic budget.
- Total project size: not stated
- Grant request: around EUR 6 million per project; other amounts may be requested and selected
- Funding form: lump sum (a fixed amount, set from a detailed budget and paid against completed work packages rather than reported costs)
Final budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 48–49 · Call ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-07), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 180–182 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-28, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 29, 32 · F — Budget flexibility; G — Budget categories

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
The single rate for all participants, including TenneT, is up to 100% of eligible costs, built into the lump sum.
- Co-financing conditions: none required by the call
For lump sum grants the funding rate is part of the method for fixing the amount and does not appear in the grant agreement.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
The grant is a lump sum fixed from a detailed budget table, which must still follow the normal cost-eligibility rules.
- Eligible costs: the detailed budget table must contain only costs that would be eligible under an actual-cost grant (personnel, subcontracting, purchases, other direct costs), because the lump sum must approximate the costs actually incurred
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs are included in the lump sum calculation at the standard 25% flat rate of direct costs (excluding subcontracting)
- Subcontracting or equipment: purchases and subcontracting must give best value for money and be free of conflicts of interest; ineligible costs in the budget table can lead to a reduced grant, even late in the project
Payment depends on completing the work packages, not on proving the costs.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, lump sum grant proposals
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 32 · G — Budget categories and cost eligibility rules

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Partners normally receive a large advance after signing, minus a 5–8% contribution to a shared insurance fund, then interim payments.
- Payment model: pre-financing (an advance) of normally 160% of the average EU funding per reporting period, then interim payments linked to periodic reports, and a final payment after the final report fixes the grant
- Retention or guarantee: 5% to 8% of the maximum grant is deducted from the pre-financing and paid into the mutual insurance mechanism (a fund covering sums that cannot be recovered from beneficiaries)
- Financial reporting or audit: depending on grant size and type of beneficiary, a certificate on the financial statements may be required; each beneficiary is liable only for its own debts
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 32–33 · G — Reporting & payment arrangements, Certificates, Liability regime for recoveries

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: full proposals are due by 1 December 2027, 17:00 Brussels time, through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Stage 1 — Full proposal: 1 December 2027, 17:00 Brussels time; Part A online and Part B of at most 28 pages (the limit for lump sum coordination and support actions), with a detailed lump sum budget table
- Opening: 4 August 2027
- Additional procedure: none; the Commission may open the call up to one month earlier or later and delay the deadline by up to two months
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 48–49 · Call ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-07), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The call sets no duration or start date: both are fixed in the grant agreement.
- Maximum duration: not set by the call; the grant agreement states the duration in months, and extensions are possible only exceptionally
- Required start: normally after the grant agreement is signed; an earlier start is possible only exceptionally, for duly justified reasons and with the granting authority's agreement
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · G — Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Indicatively, the evaluation result comes about 5 months after the deadline and the grant agreement is signed about 8 months after it.
- Funding decision: about 5 months after the deadline (indicative), around May 2028
- Grant agreement: about 8 months after the deadline (indicative)
- Conditions before starting: an invitation to grant preparation is not yet a funding commitment, since legal entity validation, financial capacity and exclusion checks follow; the partners must sign a written consortium agreement
cards.sources:

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The proposal must be complete, submitted electronically before the deadline, and within the page limit; incomplete applications are rejected.
- Application form: Part A (administrative data and a summary budget, filled in online) and Part B (the technical description, uploaded as a PDF) through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, using the forms inside the submission system; Part B is limited to 28 pages
- Budget: the summary budget in Part A and a detailed budget table, which is the basis for the lump sum
- Mandatory annexes: a plan for the exploitation and dissemination of results, including communication activities, and the ethics self-assessment
- Partner documents: the coordinator confirms at submission that it has the mandate to act for all applicants; every participant signs a declaration of honour before the grant is signed
- Registration: every beneficiary, affiliated entity and associated partner needs a participant identification code (PIC, a number from the EU Participant Register) before submission; validation of beneficiaries follows at grant preparation
- Parallel submission: none
- Lump sum: the detailed budget table is mandatory and is used to fix the lump sum
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Entities eligible to participate
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Ethics
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Independent experts score three criteria out of 5; a proposal needs 3 on each and 10 in total.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (clear, pertinent objectives; quality of the coordination and support measures), Impact (credible pathways to the expected outcomes; dissemination and exploitation measures) and Quality and efficiency of the implementation (work plan, risks, resources, capacity of each partner)
- Thresholds: at least 3 out of 5 for each criterion and 10 out of 15 overall
- Ranking rules: equal scores are separated by coverage of aspects not otherwise covered, then Excellence, then Impact, then gender balance and geographical diversity
- Budget assessment: comments on the lump sum budget table are given to proposals invited to grant preparation and to those rejected for significant over- or underestimation of costs
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 24, 26 · D — Award criteria, Scores and weighting
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 28 · F — Evaluation procedure and ranking

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
The lump sum budget, the communication-network restriction and the satellite-data rule apply in addition to the general rules.
- Exception — high-risk suppliers of mobile network communication equipment: excluded from all roles, as are entities they own or control
- Conditional — satellite data: if satellite earth observation, positioning, navigation or timing data are used, Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS must be used
- Exception — lump sum: the grant is fixed in advance from the detailed budget table instead of reimbursing reported costs
- Recommended: contribute to BRIDGE and take part in its activities
